title: Crimped weft capacitors: weave 3D DRAM's lateral capacitors over posts
idea: Borrow the crimp of woven cloth. In a stacked 3D DRAM tier, the horizontal capacitor is coated like a yarn (Ru core, HZO/ZrO2 sheath, TiN outer shell) and snakes over and under a comb of sacrificial vertical 'warp' posts that are removed afterward. The crimped path packs 1.3-1.6x more electrode length into the same tier footprint.
why: Fact 2: the lateral capacitor is what blocks 3D DRAM. ~1.5x Cs per cell cuts the tiers needed to break even from ~26 toward ~18.

title: Swiss-roll capacitor: self-rolled film-capacitor winding inside each cell
idea: Copy how wound film capacitors are made, at nanoscale. Deposit a strained TiN/ZrO2/TiN/ZrO2 nanomembrane on a sacrificial layer and release it, so built-in stress rolls it into a 3-4 turn spiral tube standing in the cell. Each winding adds electrode area without etching a 70:1 hole.
why: Facts 1 and 4: a stress-driven roll replaces the costly high-AR capacitor etch. Target is 5 fF at an equivalent AR of ~20.

title: Lost-wax gyroid: cast interpenetrating electrodes in block-copolymer molds
idea: Use investment casting. A block-copolymer double gyroid self-assembles in the capacitor trench as the 'wax'. ALD fills one network with TiN, the polymer is burned out, and ZrO2 plus a counter electrode fill the second network, leaving two interpenetrating 3D electrodes at ~10 nm periodicity.
why: Fact 1: a gyroid has 3-5x the area of a cylinder per footprint. It reaches 5 fF at much lower AR, so pillars no longer bend and kill yield.

title: Seed-pulled single-crystal SrTiO3 capacitor via lateral epitaxial overgrowth
idea: Borrow Czochralski seeding. Open a window to a single-crystal SrRuO3 seed and grow SrTiO3 laterally over the bottom electrode as one crystal, the way GaN is overgrown laterally, instead of as a fine-grained film. Removing grain boundaries removes leakage paths and suppresses the dead layer that holds polycrystalline STO to k~100.
why: Fact 1: k of ~250-300 in 8 nm films is 5-6x today's ZrO2. Capacitor AR could drop from ~70:1 to ~15:1.

title: Fermented magnetosome bits: bacteria grow uniform magnetite memory crystals
idea: Magnetotactic bacteria grow 35 nm single-domain Fe3O4 crystals with <10% size spread, uniformity that sputter-and-etch cannot match. The crystals are harvested, given DNA linkers and docked into lithographic sites on Pt or W spin-orbit-torque lines. Each bit is held as magnetization and read through magnetite's half-metallic tunneling.
why: Spin storage with unlimited endurance and no MTJ etch damage. The fab tool is a fermenter, which cuts capital intensity, and pitch is ~50 nm for nonvolatile working memory.

title: Conveyor-belt CCD loops: charge packets recirculate, no capacitor per bit
idea: Treat memory as an assembly line. Bits are charge packets clocked around closed buried-channel CCD rings of 64-256 wells, and each ring has a single sense/regenerate station, so every lap is a refresh. No bit has its own access transistor or capacitor, only overlapping gates.
why: Facts 1, 3 and 7: the capacitor and access-transistor leakage are gone. A bit costs ~4F2 of gate and the periphery is shared across a whole ring. Fits streamed pages such as KV cache, with <=64 ns rotation latency.

title: Electroplated pseudocapacitor bit: hydrous RuO2 stores charge as surface protons
idea: Use electroplating to fill each shallow cup with hydrous RuO2.xH2O. Charge is held by fast surface proton redox (pseudocapacitance) rather than a dielectric, ~10-50x a dielectric capacitor per real area. A thin solid proton conductor is the separator.
why: Fact 1: 5 fF from a cup of AR ~5-10, so no deep capacitor etch. The main risk is whether the redox kinetics reach ns.

title: Die-cast gallium droplet bit: liquid metal shuttles between two wells
idea: Borrow metal casting. A ~10 nm Ga-alloy droplet is sealed in a dumbbell-shaped nano-cavity, and electrocapillary pulses move it from one lobe to the other, where surface tension holds it (bistable). A sense electrode reads the position as a capacitance change.
why: Mechanical storage with no leakage, so no refresh (fact 3). A liquid cannot fatigue, so endurance is effectively unlimited and the state holds with no power.

title: Zone-refining domain walls: LiNbO3 conducting walls as nondestructive bits
idea: A zone-refining heater sweeps a molten zone through a bar. Here a short pulse sweeps a ferroelectric domain wall across a tiny single-crystal LiNbO3 mesa made by thin-film ion slicing. The bit is whether a conductive wall bridges the electrodes, read as a uA wall current without switching polarization.
why: Fact 8: read is nondestructive with a large current signal and no capacitor. Writes take <10 ns, and single-crystal film gives endurance far above HZO.

title: Prestressed magnetoelectric bit: tempered-glass stress makes strain-switched magnets bistable
idea: Copy tempered and prestressed glass: build a permanent biaxial stress into a Terfenol-D (TbDyFe) nanomagnet on a PMN-PT piezo pillar. The prestress creates two stable easy axes at +/-45 degrees, and a voltage pulse strains the magnet from one to the other. A tunnel junction reads it.
why: Fact 10: written by voltage with no current, at ~1 aJ instead of fJ-scale CV2. Nonvolatile, so refresh energy disappears.

title: Photographic latent-image bit: few silver atoms hold a few electrons
idea: Silver-halide film keeps a stable 4-atom Ag cluster as the latent image, which development later amplifies. Here sub-3 nm Ag clusters self-assembled in an oxide each hold 1-5 electrons behind a Coulomb-blockade barrier. An integrated single-electron transistor 'develops' the latent charge on read.
why: Fact 1: about 5 electrons replace 5 fF (~30k electrons), cutting write charge and CV2 energy ~1000x. The high charging energy makes tunneling-out, and so refresh, rare.

title: Macrame hopfions: knotted spin textures stacked as beads in one pillar
idea: Borrow knot-tying. Current pulses write 3D knotted magnetic solitons (hopfions) into a thick Co/Pt/Ir multilayer pillar, several stacked vertically like knots on a cord. Each level's presence or absence is a bit, read by depth-resolved magnetoresistance from a segmented pillar.
why: Fact 2: multi-bit 3D storage in one etched pillar with no transistor tiers. Topological protection gives unlimited endurance at ~4 bits per 4F2 footprint.

title: Check-valve bottling: resonant-tunnel barrier seals a quantum-well charge
idea: Like a bottle with a one-way valve cap, an InAs quantum well holds charge behind an InAs/AlSb triple barrier. The barrier is opaque at rest (~2.1 eV AlSb offset) and turns resonantly transparent only near 2.5 V, filling or emptying the well in ns.
why: Fact 3: retention of hours to years nearly removes refresh while writes stay fast and low-energy. It also gives U.S. III-V fabs a memory product.

title: Puff-pastry laminated HfO2/ZrO2 tuned to the morphotropic boundary
idea: Laminate like puff pastry folds dough: ALD supercycles stack 0.5 nm HfO2/ZrO2 leaves whose interface strain pins the film at the tetragonal-orthorhombic morphotropic phase boundary. There, field-induced polarization rotation peaks permittivity at k~60-70 without full ferroelectric switching.
why: Fact 1 directly: k~70 is the stated alternative to AR 115. Cs rises 2-3x at the same AR, and since the film never fully switches, endurance stays effectively unlimited.

title: Offset-printed alpha-In2Se3 sheets: ferroelectric semiconductor channel holds the bit
idea: Like offset printing transfers ink from a blanket roller, a wafer-scale stamp transfers MBE-grown alpha-In2Se3 layers onto the logic wafer. The bit is polarization inside the semiconductor channel itself, so no separate ferroelectric gate is needed, and channel conductance reads it non-destructively.
why: Facts 1 and 8: no capacitor and no destructive read. vdW layers lack the oxygen-vacancy fatigue path, so endurance aims at 1e12+, and BEOL transfer avoids front-end capital.

title: Hot-foil stamping bit: single heat pulse toggles a GdFeCo magnet
idea: A hot-foil stamp transfers its image with one heat pulse. In the same way, a ~10 ps current pulse heats a GdFeCo ferrimagnet nanodot, and ultrafast Gd/Fe sublattice exchange toggles its magnetization with no field, no spin torque and no polarity. An MTJ on top reads it.
why: DRAM-class (ps) write speed in a nonvolatile cell with unlimited endurance. Simple toggle drivers cut refresh and periphery (facts 3 and 7).

title: Movable-type memory: one standard storage-element socket, swappable bit physics
idea: Like Gutenberg's interchangeable type in one press, define an open hybrid-bond 'socket': a fixed periphery and sense wafer with a standard 0.5 um-pitch bond pad per sub-array plus fixed voltage, timing and signal windows. Any new storage-element wafer (capacitor, ferroelectric, magnetic) bonds on and is tested with no periphery redesign.
why: Fact 7 and capital intensity: a new bit physics becomes a wafer swap rather than a $1B program. Trial cost drops ~10-50x and the periphery stays on a mature node.

title: Yuba-skimmed dielectric: peel atomically thin oxide skins off liquid metal
idea: Copy yuba (tofu-skin) making. A Ga-Hf liquid alloy grows a self-limiting HfO2-rich oxide skin ~1 nm thick, and touching a wafer to the surface prints that skin, pinhole-free, as the capacitor dielectric at near-room temperature.
why: Fact 1: a near-perfect 1 nm high-k skin gives EOT ~0.2 nm, about 3x capacitance per area for planar plates in stacked 3D tiers. The low temperature allows BEOL stacking.

title: Williams-tube revival: field-emitter arrays write charge spots on dielectric
idea: The 1940s Williams tube stored bits as charge spots on a CRT face. Its nanoscale successor is a vacuum-sealed array of Spindt field-emission tips, each deflecting its beam over an 8x8 field of spots to write and read electron charge in a trap-rich dielectric film. The bit lives in the film, with no access transistor.
why: Facts 3 and 4: the storage medium is an unpatterned film, so no transistor or litho-defined capacitor is needed per cell. Vacuum-isolated traps cut refresh, and the cost moves into emitter arrays.

title: Splat-quenched charge-density-wave bit in 1T-TaS2 nanoflakes
idea: Use the splat quenching that makes metallic glass. A 30 ps current pulse melts the charge-density-wave order of a 1T-TaS2 flake and refreezes it into a metastable 'hidden' metallic state, and a longer gentle pulse restores the insulating state. The bit is the electronic phase, read as a 10-100x resistance ratio.
why: A purely electronic phase change: no atoms move, so endurance is unlimited (unlike PCM), and switching is ps at fJ energy. The risk is keeping the state stable near room temperature through strain and thickness.

title: Glow-pigment trap bit: persistent-phosphor traps read by stimulated light
idea: Borrow glow-in-the-dark SrAl2O4:Eu,Dy pigment manufacturing. A co-packaged photonic die writes a bit by trapping electrons at Dy traps in phosphor nanodots on plasmonic antennas, and reads it by optically stimulated luminescence into an on-die SPAD. Co-dopant chemistry sets the trap depth and thus the retention.
why: Facts 5 and 3: the trap does not wear, so endurance is unlimited. Minutes of retention cut refresh ~1000x and optical read allows photonic links, but antennas limit density to ~50 nm pitch.

title: Paper-mill layered magnet: gated vdW ferromagnet spin-filter tunnel bit
idea: Like pressing paper sheets, stack a few layers of the room-temperature vdW ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2 with hBN. A gate pulse switches interlayer coupling between ferro and antiferro alignment, and spin-filter tunneling changes the current by >100x.
why: Fact 10: a magnetic bit set by voltage, not current, at aJ energy. The giant read signal allows small sense amps (fact 7), and it is nonvolatile, so no refresh.

title: Bead-strung vortex cores: nanoring magnets threaded on vertical wires
idea: Revive hand-strung core memory: deposit ~40 nm permalloy nanorings as 'beads' around vertical metal pillar 'strings'. Pillar current writes clockwise or counterclockwise vortex chirality by Oersted field, and the flux-closed rings have no stray field, so 4-8 can stack on one pillar and be read through a ring-segment MTJ.
why: Fact 2: multi-bit vertical stacking on a single pillar with no per-bit transistor. Zero stray field packs bits densely, with unlimited endurance.

title: MLCC-in-a-pillar: tape-cast style Ni/BaTiO3 multilayer cell capacitor
idea: Shrink multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC) manufacturing into each cell. A pillar holds 20 alternating Ni/BaTiO3 5 nm layers, like co-fired MLCC sheets, with odd layers recessed on one sidewall and even layers on the other, so a storage-node contact and a plate contact each reach every other electrode.
why: Fact 1: 6 fF from a pillar of AR ~7 instead of 70, using only Ni, Ba, Ti and O. MLCC makers already co-process Ni/BaTiO3 at enormous volume.

title: Anodized-aluminum capacitor forest: self-ordered 1000:1 pores without etching
idea: Copy architectural aluminum anodizing. Sputter 1 um of Al over the transistor array, imprint dimples aligned to the storage contacts, and anodize at ~10 V in sulfuric acid so pores self-order at ~25 nm pitch, one per dimple. ALD then lines each pore with TiN/TiO2-Al2O3/TiN.
why: Facts 4 and 1: a wet electrochemical bath with near-zero tool cost replaces the most expensive high-AR capacitor etch. AR >100 becomes trivial, giving >10 fF even at k~30.

title: Raney-nickel sponge electrode: dealloy Ni-Al to multiply capacitor area
idea: Use the way Raney nickel catalyst is made. Deposit Ni-Al alloy in each shallow cup and leach the Al out with NaOH, leaving a nanoporous Ni sponge with ~5 nm ligaments that ALD then coats with Al2O3/ZrO2 dielectric and a TiN counter electrode.
why: Fact 1: 10-20x internal area per footprint makes 5 fF at AR ~5. Ni, Al, Zr, Ti and O replace Ru, Hf and W electrodes and liners.

title: Preform-drawn coax capacitor wafers: draw, bundle, redraw, then slice
idea: Borrow optical-fiber drawing. Build a macroscopic preform (Zn-Sn alloy core, BaTiO3-loaded glass dielectric, metal outer shell), then thermally draw, stack and redraw it down to ~30 nm cores. Wafer-thin slices of the bundle carry billions of parallel coax capacitors, which are hybrid-bonded onto the transistor wafer.
why: Fact 1 and capital intensity: capacitor length equals slice thickness (um), not an etched hole, so each coax exceeds 5 fF with no litho or etch. A draw tower replaces a fab for the capacitor wafer.

title: Diatom-fermented silica sponge, magnesium-reduced into porous silicon electrodes
idea: Diatoms build nanoporous silica using silaffin peptides. Here those peptides precipitate biosilica conformally inside each cup at room temperature from silicic acid, and magnesiothermic reduction (2Mg + SiO2 -> Si + 2MgO, MgO washed out) turns it into doped porous silicon, which TiO2/Al2O3 then coats to form the capacitor.
why: Fact 1 and scarce resources: a high-area storage electrode (target 5-8x area) from water, silica chemistry and magnesium. No Ru or W precursors and no deep etch.

title: Lab-grown-gem diamond storage node: 5.5 eV bandgap kills leakage tail
idea: Borrow CVD gem growth to make single-crystal diamond tiles (carbon only). The storage node is a boron-doped diamond junction capacitor with a hydrogen-terminated diamond access FET, and intrinsic carrier generation is ~1e-36 of silicon's, so retention runs to hours.
why: Fact 3: the <=13 fA leakage tail drops to effectively zero, removing the 16-33% of idle power and 10-20% of bandwidth that refresh costs. Diamond is pure carbon, and CVD reactors are small and buildable in the U.S.

title: Chocolate-tempered rutile TiO2: seed crystals select the k~100 polymorph
idea: Chocolatiers add Form-V cocoa-butter seed crystals to force the right crystal form. Here a 2 nm rutile-structured beta-MnO2 (or F:SnO2) seed on a TiN electrode, plus a tempering anneal cycle, forces TiO2 to crystallize as rutile (k~90-110) instead of anatase (k~40) at <=450 C, with no RuO2 template.
why: Fact 1: about 2-2.5x today's ZrO2 k using only Ti, Mn and O. Removes the Ru dependence of rutile-TiO2 DRAM capacitors.

title: Bimetallic-strip negative-capacitance capacitor: ferroelectric AlBN fights linear Al2O3
idea: A thermostat's bimetallic strip pairs two opposing layers to get a new behavior. Here a wurtzite ferroelectric Al(1-x)B(x)N layer sits in series with Al2O3 dielectric, matched so the ferroelectric's negative-capacitance region is stabilized and never switches, lifting total capacitance above that of the Al2O3 alone.
why: Facts 1 and 10: capacitance rises 2-3x, and the charge gain lets VARY fall toward 0.6 V. Only Al, B, N and O, with no Hf or Zr.

title: Softgel nanocapsule: sealed ionic-liquid double-layer capacitor per cell
idea: Use pharmaceutical softgel encapsulation: fill each cup with an imidazolium ionic liquid (C, H, N, O, S, F) and seal it under an ALD Al2O3 lid. Charge sits in the ~1 nm electric double layer at carbon or TiN electrodes, at ~15-20 uF/cm2 (10-20x an oxide dielectric) and ~ns RC at 10 nm scale.
why: Fact 1: 5 fF from an AR ~8 cup. Inside the electrochemical window there is no dielectric tunneling leakage, and the materials are commodity organics.

title: Dye-bath ferrocene grafting: quantized multi-level molecular charge storage
idea: Copy textile mordant dyeing: dip the wafer so the cup walls graft a mixed monolayer of ferrocene and biferrocene derivatives (Fe, C, H). Their distinct redox potentials store charge in discrete plateaus (2 bits per cell), and leakage cannot drift a level until a whole plateau has emptied.
why: Fact 3: quantized levels tolerate the leakage tail, allowing ~10x longer refresh intervals and 2 bits per cell. Iron-based chemistry needs no scarce metals.

title: Coin-stamped snap-dome bit: bistable buckled SiC membrane holds data
idea: Borrow keyboard snap-dome stamping: nanoimprint-coin a 40 nm SiC (or diamond-like-carbon) dome with built-in compressive stress over a vacuum cavity, so it is stable bowed up or bowed down. Electrostatic electrodes snap it in ~1-5 ns, and dome position shifts a capacitance on the sense line.
why: Facts 3 and 9: mechanical storage has zero leakage, so no refresh, and there is no stored charge to row-hammer. Si and C only, and SiC membranes are rated beyond 1e12 cycles.

title: Bell-cast parametron: AlN nano-resonator stores bits as oscillation phase
idea: Revive Goto's parametron using a bell-founder's resonator. A shared 2f pump drives an AlN/Si nanobeam, which rings at f in one of two phases (0 or pi), and that phase is the bit. A small seed signal writes it, phase comparison against a reference reads it, and one global pump powers millions of cells.
why: Facts 10 and 3: energy recirculates in a high-Q (~1e4) resonance, escaping the CV2 floor. No leakage tail, and only Al, N and Si.

title: Knitted MgB2 persistent-current loops for a cryogenic memory tier
idea: Interlock superconducting MgB2 loops like knitting (Tc 39 K, Mg and B only). Each loop holds a bit as a circulating persistent current, a flux quantum in or out, switched and sensed by an MgB2 nano-bridge, forming a 20 K cryocooled memory tier beside cryogenic AI accelerators.
why: Facts 3 and 10: zero static power, no refresh and aJ switching, ~1e6x below DRAM write energy. Cryocooler capital buys freedom from exotic metals.

title: Gun-bluing rust bit: oxidized-iron antiferromagnet switched by orbital torque
idea: Borrow gun bluing, the controlled oxidation of steel: thermally oxidize Fe films into epitaxial alpha-Fe2O3 (hematite) nanodots whose Neel vector is the bit. A Cr/CuOx line underneath switches it by orbital Hall torque, and spin-Hall magnetoresistance reads it.
why: Antiferromagnets have no stray field (<=10 nm pitch) and THz dynamics (sub-ns write). Unlimited endurance and no refresh from iron rust, chromium and copper, with no Pt, Co or Ta.

title: Shape-memory 'training' bit: Ni-Mn-Sn martensite twin variant stores data
idea: Copy how shape-memory-alloy wire is trained: train a Ni-Mn-Sn Heusler nanodot so its martensite settles in one of two twin variants. Gate-applied strain or field flips the variant diffusionlessly, with no atomic migration, and magnetic or resistive anisotropy reads it.
why: Ferroelastic storage from Ni, Mn and Sn with no charge leakage (fact 3). Diffusionless switching aims at >1e12 cycles.

title: Thermochromic-ink spin-crossover bit: Fe-triazole molecules hold spin state
idea: Borrow thermochromic ink printing: a film of [Fe(Htrz)2(trz)](BF4) spin-crossover complex (Fe, C, H, N, B, F) sits inside its room-temperature thermal hysteresis loop. A ns heat or field pulse flips molecules between high and low spin, and the ~10% volume and dielectric change is read capacitively or through a strain-gated channel.
why: Bistable molecular storage needing no refresh (fact 3), solution-printable from cents of iron and organics. Write energy is the latent heat of a 20 nm dot, ~fJ.

title: Rock-candy croconic acid: proton-hopping organic ferroelectric bit
idea: Like rock candy growing on a seeded string, croconic acid (C5H2O5) crystallizes from vapor onto seed lines between TiN electrodes. It is a room-temperature ferroelectric whose polarization flips by proton transfer along hydrogen bonds, read through a ferroelectric tunnel junction.
why: ~20 uC/cm2 polarization from C, H and O alone, with low coercive field (targets fact 10's voltage floor). Proton tautomerism has no oxygen-vacancy fatigue path.

title: One-drop-fill ferroelectric nematic: fluid polar bit that cannot fatigue
idea: Use LCD one-drop-fill manufacturing: dispense a ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (RM734/DIO class: C, H, N, O, F) into sealed nano-cells whose antiparallel polar surface anchoring makes the ~5 uC/cm2 polarization bistable. A low-voltage pulse flips it in ns, and a capacitive charge read senses it.
why: Fact 10 and endurance: a fluid ferroelectric self-heals and does not wear out, with polarization comparable to solid ferroelectrics from commodity organics. The fill process is borrowed from the LCD industry.

title: Veneer-stacked hBN: sliding ferroelectric bit from boron and nitrogen
idea: Like plywood veneers laid at controlled grain angles, stack two hBN monolayers in parallel (AB/BA) alignment so out-of-plane polarization flips with a one-third-lattice interlayer slide. A graphene channel underneath reads it non-destructively as a resistance shift.
why: Facts 8 and 10: non-destructive read and near-fatigue-free sliding switching at <1 V, from B, N and C only. Being atomically thin, it fits monolithic 3D tiers.

title: Bookbinding signatures: capacitors printed on a cheap 200 mm wafer
idea: Bind memory like a book: a U.S. 200 mm foundry prints the capacitor array as a separate 'signature' wafer, using i-line litho and Earth-abundant AAO or Ni/BaTiO3 capacitors, and sells it as a merchant product. It is wafer-to-wafer hybrid-bonded face-to-face onto transistor wafers from a leading-edge fab.
why: Fact 4 and U.S. manufacturability: ~40% of DRAM process steps move off EUV-class lines onto depreciated, idle 200 mm capacity, cutting capital per bit ~30%.

title: Zeolite autoclave cages: trapped sodium ion hops between two sites
idea: Use hydrothermal autoclave zeolite synthesis to grow sodalite films (Na, Al, Si, O) in the cell, where each cage holds a Na+ ion in a double-well site. A field pulse shifts the caged ions to one side as a bistable dipolar polarization, and the displacement charge is read.
why: Fact 3: ion-hop barriers of ~1 eV mean minutes-to-years retention with no electronic leakage path. The elements are Earth's most abundant, and the rigid cage framework means unlimited endurance.

title: Thermite-foil flash anneal: reactive Al/Ni layers crystallize BaTiO3 in-cell
idea: Borrow the reactive multilayer foils used for soldering: cap the capacitor stack with a 20 nm Al/Ni nanolaminate and ignite it with a pulse. The self-propagating reaction delivers a ~1 ns, >1000 C local heat spike that crystallizes the BaTiO3/SrTiO3 dielectric into high-k perovskite while the transistors below stay under 400 C.
why: Fact 1: crystalline perovskite at k ~200+ becomes BEOL-compatible without a high-thermal-budget anneal, and the NiAl product becomes the top electrode. Only Al, Ni, Ba, Sr, Ti and O.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor 'forming': self-healing anodic Al2O3 kills leakage tail
idea: Copy the forming step of aluminum electrolytic capacitors: each cell has an anodic Al2O3 dielectric under a conductive polymer (PEDOT: C, H, O, S) counter electrode. A periodic forming voltage re-anodizes weak spots, and the polymer over hot spots de-dopes into an insulator, so leaky outlier cells cure themselves instead of setting the refresh rate.
why: Fact 3: refresh is set by the worst ~ppm leakage tail. Self-healing compresses that tail ~10x (refresh 64 ms -> ~0.5 s) using Al and organics only.
